segments.text: Gumgumi stands in the cold yard and breathes out.
Even indoors, warm breath has water vapor in it.
But strangely, it only looks white outside.
Breath warms up inside you and picks up water vapor.
That warm breath meets cold air and cools instantly.
Cooler air can't hold it all, so it forms tiny droplets.
The droplets scatter light everywhere, so it looks white.
Back in the yard, the breath still looks white.
Warm breath cools into droplets, and that looks white.
